description:
Routing probes for all 32 acs skills. Every skill is model-invocable, so routing is measurable for all of them. 24 get one natural-language request that must route to them without naming them. `install-hooks` and `update` are user actions rather than pipeline steps, so each gets two positives: the explicit command and the natural-language request. The six INTERNAL legs -- `workflows/phases.yaml`'s `internal` map: `create-project`, `standardize-project`, and the four ADR-0095 delivery-path legs `code-trivial`, `code-small`, `code-standard` and `code-complex` -- get a pair each: an explicit invocation that MUST route, because a leg is dispatched and resumed by name, and a bare description of its intent that must NOT, because only its entry point (`/acs:project`, `/acs:code`) may answer that.

This file is the curated data. runner/gen_plugin_eval.py renders it into plugins/acs/evals/routing/<case>/ as prompt.md plus graders/*.md, the format https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugin-evals specifies. Nothing pins the routing SURFACE deterministically any more: dataset/cases/10-skills.json did, and went with the rest of the no-model tier.

Three CONTROL probes test the instrument rather than the plugin: a registration canary that must hit, an unregistered command that must miss, and an off-domain request that must route nowhere. Without them a suite where nothing can pass and one where nothing can fail are indistinguishable from a pass count. Controls are not rendered into `claude plugin eval` cases. A probe may name the sandbox `profile` it runs in (default `ticketed`) and deterministic `setup` shell steps run once before its first session, so the prompt's presupposition holds — a prompt about "this existing codebase" is no test of a description on an empty seeded repo.

probes.prompt: Before we plan anything for TKT-1, work out what it really asks for: what breaks, what is unclear, and what we are assuming.
probes.why: A natural-language request in the skill's domain, never naming the skill. Deliberately pre-plan: the neighbour is create-impl-plan, so the prompt asks for understanding and open questions, never for an approach or a file list.

probes.prompt: TKT-1 already has approved specs in the workspace. Please implement it.
probes.why: A natural-language request in the skill's domain, never naming the skill.

probes.prompt: /acs:code-trivial
probes.why: The explicit command must keep resolving: a delivery-path leg is invoked directly to resume an interrupted /acs:code run on the trivial path. The leg is dispatched by /acs:code, never chosen by a user from a description (ADR-0095 judges the path from plan.md), so this probe covers the one invocation that is legitimately explicit.

probes.prompt: TKT-1's plan is approved and it is a trivial two-line change. Implement it.
probes.why: A request to implement an approved plan must reach /acs:code, the entry point, even when the user's own wording names the trivial path: which leg runs is read from the ticket's recorded `delivery_path`, judged once from the plan (ADR-0095), never inferred from how the request is phrased. This probe deliberately plants the word a mis-grab would key on, so the leg's DESCRIPTION — dispatched by /acs:code, never chosen by hand — is what has to hold.

probes.prompt: The plan for TKT-1 adds two new endpoints. Pin down their request and response shapes, the error codes and the compatibility story before anything is built.
probes.why: A natural-language request in the skill's domain, never naming the skill. The neighbour is create-impl-plan; the prompt is scoped to the external surface and its shapes rather than to the internal approach.

probes.prompt: We have a PRD now. Draw up the system architecture docs — the C4 views and the key flows.
probes.why: A natural-language request in the skill's domain, never naming the skill.

probes.prompt: TKT-1 is design-significant. Settle its system design and weigh the options before anyone writes code.
probes.why: A natural-language request in the skill's domain, never naming the skill. 1.6.0 fixes both halves of a 3/5 split on the 2026-09-13 measurement, neither of them the description's. The prompt said "this epic" and named none: a diagnostic caught the model identifying the right skill ("this matches /acs:create-design exactly") and then declining for want of a referent — "I need to know which epic you mean". It now names the ticket, as ROUTE-create-test-docs and ROUTE-run-e2e-tests already do. And the sandbox is now `epic`: the default `ticketed` profile mints a small, low-stakes TASK, so "design-significant" was false of the only ticket present, while `epic` mints a large, high-stakes epic — exactly what the prompt describes.

probes.prompt: Bootstrap the quality and operations doc sets together, in parallel rather than one after the other.
probes.why: A natural-language request in the skill's domain, never naming the skill.

probes.prompt: TKT-1's test plan has three end-to-end cases and none of them exist yet. Write those suites on the ticket branch.
probes.why: A natural-language request in the skill's domain, never naming the skill. The neighbours are create-test-docs and run-e2e-tests; the prompt presupposes the cases already exist and asks for the suites to be authored, not run.

probes.why: A natural-language request in the skill's domain, never naming the skill. Deliberately post-analysis and pre-code: the neighbours are analyze-ticket and code, so the prompt asks for the approach, not for understanding or edits.

probes.why: A natural-language request in the skill's domain, never naming the skill.

probes.prompt: I want to define this product properly: vision, the problem, personas, goals with measurable success metrics.
probes.why: A natural-language request in the skill's domain, never naming the skill.

probes.prompt: /acs:create-project
probes.why: The explicit command must keep resolving: a user invokes a leg directly to resume an interrupted delivery ticket, which is what its argument-hint offers. This probe used to be justified by disable-model-invocation — "only an explicit invocation may route" — which is no longer true of any skill; it now pins registration, decided at the init event like every other explicit probe.

probes.prompt: This repo is brand new and empty. Scaffold the project skeleton from the approved architecture.
probes.why: A plain description of the leg's own subject must NOT reach the leg: /acs:project is the documented front door and is what should pick it up. What delivers that is the leg's DESCRIPTION ("Internal leg of /acs:project, not a user-facing command"), not a frontmatter flag. Until 2026-09-13 the leg set disable-model-invocation, which the CLI enforces by refusing the Skill call — and /acs:project dispatches this leg with a real Skill(acs:create-project) call, so the flag stopped the fold working at all. The probe is unchanged; only its justification is.

probes.prompt: Reverse-engineer the functional and non-functional requirements out of this existing codebase.
probes.why: A natural-language request in the skill's domain, never naming the skill. 1.5.0: runs on the fixture app — the prompt presupposes a codebase to reverse-engineer, and on the empty seeded repo the model inspected it, found nothing, and asked instead of routing (1/5 runs).

probes.prompt: Work out the test cases TKT-1 needs from its acceptance criteria, and say which suite each one belongs in.
probes.why: A natural-language request in the skill's domain, never naming the skill. The neighbours are create-e2e-tests and run-e2e-tests; the prompt asks for the cases to be derived and written down, never for suites to be authored or run.

probes.prompt: We need a ticket for adding SSO login to the customer portal.
probes.why: A natural-language request in the skill's domain, never naming the skill.

probes.prompt: The code change is done. Make sure the docs match what actually changed before we raise the PR.
probes.why: A natural-language request in the skill's domain, never naming the skill. The prompt presupposes a finished change the docs do not yet describe, so the sandbox has to contain one. 1.5.0 committed an UNREFERENCED constant under a commit message claiming the routes were added; the model read the diff, found do_GET/do_POST untouched, concluded docs/api.md's "the API is read-and-create only" was still accurate, and declined to sync — correctly. It split 3/5 on the 2026-09-13 measurement and 2/5 on a 5-run diagnostic, every miss for that reason. 1.6.0 commits the real handler: POST /orders/<id>/confirm and /pay now dispatch to the service, so the documented claim is genuinely false and there is something to sync.
setup: git commit -qam 'TKT-1 let the API confirm and pay an order'

probes.prompt: I need to stop here. Park this ticket cleanly so I can pick it up in a fresh session tomorrow.
probes.why: A natural-language request in the skill's domain, never naming the skill.

probes.prompt: /acs:install-hooks
probes.why: The explicit command must keep resolving. Previously justified by disable-model-invocation ("only an explicit invocation may route"); it now pins registration, decided at the init event, alongside the description probe that was this skill's negative case.

probes.prompt: Set up the git hooks for this repository so checks run before every commit.
probes.why: A natural-language request in the skill's domain, never naming the skill. This was a NEGATIVE probe until 2026-09-13, asserting that disable-model-invocation kept the model from reaching acs:install-hooks. No skill sets that flag now, so the same prompt states the opposite and better claim: a request about local git hooks should reach this skill. The prompt is unchanged.

probes.prompt: The PR is approved and CI is green. Land it and clean up the branch.
probes.why: A natural-language request in the skill's domain, never naming the skill.

probes.prompt: Show me our delivery throughput — how many tickets are done, and how the pipeline is converting.
probes.why: A natural-language request in the skill's domain, never naming the skill.

probes.prompt: This repository has no build or test tooling yet. Set up its structure so work can start.
probes.why: A natural-language request in the skill's domain, never naming the skill. The umbrella auto-detects greenfield versus existing; the prompt states the greenfield evidence so the routing decision, not the mode decision, is measured.

probes.prompt: Cut version 0.4.10: assemble the changelog section and open the release PR.
probes.why: A natural-language request in the skill's domain, never naming the skill.

probes.prompt: Execute the end-to-end suites for TKT-1 and tell me which of its cases passed.
probes.why: A natural-language request in the skill's domain, never naming the skill. The neighbour is create-e2e-tests, and the alias `test` shares the domain; the prompt asks for execution and results, never for authoring.

probes.prompt: Configure acs for this repository — ticket prefix, coverage target, merge strategy.
probes.why: A natural-language request in the skill's domain, never naming the skill.

probes.prompt: TKT-1 is ready to go. Take it from here to a pull request for me — I don't want to drive each step myself.
probes.why: A natural-language request in the skill's domain, never naming the skill. The prompt names a TICKET, because a ticket is what the skill takes: since the skills-independence refactor /acs:ship parses its argument as "a ticket id, and nothing else" and refuses a bare prompt, redirecting to /acs:create-ticket. The 1.3.0 prompt asked for a password-reset flow to be shipped from nothing and routed to acs:create-ticket on 5/5 runs of the 2026-09-13 measurement — the documented correct answer to a prompt carrying no ticket. That probe was measuring a contract the plugin no longer has.

probes.why: A natural-language request in the skill's domain, never naming the skill. This was a NEGATIVE probe until 2026-09-13, asserting that disable-model-invocation kept the model from reaching acs:update. No skill sets that flag now, so the same prompt states the opposite and better claim: a request about a newer plugin version should reach this skill. The prompt is unchanged.

probes.prompt: How much have we spent on AI for this repo, and what's the token burn per role?
probes.why: A natural-language request in the skill's domain, never naming the skill.

probes.prompt: Write a four-line poem about the sea.
probes.why: A request with nothing to do with software delivery must invoke no skill at all. Routing it anywhere is over-triggering by the plugin's descriptions; reporting a skill here when none fired is a lying detector. Either way the surrounding measurement cannot be read.

probes.prompt: /acs:setup
probes.why: Deterministic canary, decided at the init event with no model turn: the CLI must list the plugin's commands. If this misses, the session cannot see the plugin at all and every paid probe would be measuring an absence — the failure that hid all 22 routes for three paid runs in September 2026. It is a control: it tests the instrument, not the plugin, so it is not rendered into a case.

probes.prompt: /acs:no-such-skill
probes.why: A detector that reported every explicit probe as registered would pass the canary and both explicit probes alike. This command does not exist, so it must miss; a hit here means the instrument is lying, not that the plugin grew a skill.

probes.prompt: Go over the changes on this branch and tell me what's wrong with them before I put it up for review — build, lint and tests included.
probes.why: A natural-language request in the skill's domain, never naming the skill. review-code carried no probe at all until the guide-format migration compared the probed set against the skills on disk.
